mentions.name: Rural co-op ISP
mentions.description: This project was a cooperative ISP spun up about a decade ago to take advantage of fiber grants for rural areas, with nearly 90% of the population across three counties on board. It struggled to get off the ground amid red tape, regulations, and a lawsuit from a large incumbent provider.
mentions.problem: Rural towns and farms lacked high-speed internet because large incumbent providers held exclusive rights and were never planning to offer anything above DSL for most people and cable for those in town.
mentions.source_excerpt: We spun up a co-op isp to take advantage of fiber grants for rural areas about a decade ago. Maybe it was because of the grants, but it was a fucking nightmare getting off the ground even though we had nearly 90% of the population in three counties on board for the co-op.
